title: Image rotation and SBOM synchronizer with CUDA pinset policy
creator: Lena Martinez
description:
Summary:
We need a resilient, auditable process that rotates container images, synchronizes SBOMs, and applies an explicit CUDA/driver pinset policy across Redwood's runtime images. The goal is to make image updates predictable, ensure SBOMs are always paired with the image they describe, and prevent unexpected driver/CUDA mismatches during rollouts to Dedicated and Private deployments. This task builds the orchestration glue (synchronizer + policy enforcement) and a rollout gate pattern that gates automated image promotion across LTS channels.

Objectives:
- Implement an SBOM synchronizer that consumes new image builds, calculates a signed SBOM delta, and attaches provenance metadata to the image registry entry.
- Create a canonical mapping (pinset) of supported CUDA driver stacks to runtime image families and expose an API/manifest that other services can query.
- Introduce a configurable image rotation workflow that: tags image candidates, runs compatibility checks (smoke+kernel sanity), gates promotion using canary percentages and health metrics, and atomically updates the image mapping used by autoscaling pools.
- Add rollout gates: health windows, observed latency/cost regressions thresholds, and deterministic fallback to prior pinned images.
- Integrate notifications into Console (rollout dashboard) and add alerts for SBOM drift, provenance mismatches, and driver-pin violations.

Non-goals:
- Replacing container build system; we will integrate with existing CI (ci.redwood) outputs.
- Rewriting kernel drivers or changing CUDA versions outside of the pinset policy process.

Acceptance criteria:
1) SBOM synchronizer service exists and consumes CI artifacts: for each image it persists an SBOM blob, creates a signed delta against previous SBOM, and writes an entry into the image-catalog with fields: image_digest, sbom_digest, sbom_delta_url, build_id, created_at.
2) Pinset manifest published at /image-policies/cuda-pinset.json includes stable mappings for image families and driver versions; the manifest is signed and versioned.
3) Image rotation workflow can promote an image across dev -> canary -> stable channels with configurable phasing (e.g., 5%/25%/100%).
4) Rollout gate prevents promotion if kernel compatibility tests or latency regressions exceed configured thresholds.
5) Console shows a rollout timeline and a link to the SBOM diff and driver pinset entry for each promoted image.

Design notes / approach:
- Synchronizer will be a small service (Go) that subscribes to 'image-created' events in our artifact bus. It will fetch the CI-generated SBOM, canonicalize it (SPDX v2 with our extension fields), compute a binary diff via existing sbom-diff tool, sign artifacts with the release key, and push metadata to the image-catalog service.
- The CUDA pinset will be a single JSON manifest with semantics: {image_family -> supported_cuda_versions -> driver_candidates}. The orchestrator consults this manifest before scheduling any nodes with the new image.
- Compatibility checks: run containerized kernel sanity suite on representative instance types (g5 / a100 variants) to ensure no runtime OOM or driver API failures. These will run as pre-promotion gates in ephemeral test pools.
- Rollout gating: use the existing rollout API (route-layer) with extended policy hooks to call a 'verify' webhook that will look up SBOM provenance, run a quick retraining of cache keys, and check canary metrics. If verification fails, automated rollback should execute within the orchestration engine.

Telemetry & monitoring:
- Emit events: sbom.ingest.success|failure, sbom.delta.generated, pinset.mismatch, rotation.promotion.attempt, rotation.promotion.success|fail, rollback.executed.
- Add Console widgets: SBOM drift rate, percentage of images with signed SBOMs, pinset mismatch rate.
- Alerting: PagerDuty on high-severity failures (promotion fail + inability to rollback), Slack notifications to #release-eng for partial failures.

Security & compliance:
- All SBOMs and delta artifacts must be signed with our release key and stored in the secure artifact store with immutability retention for 90 days.
- Since this touches driver pinning, include an explicit review with Security (see links below) and add a precondition that LTS-channel promotions require security_approval = true.

Rollout plan (high level):
1) Deploy SBOM synchronizer in staging and validate with synthetic CI artifacts.
2) Publish initial CUDA pinset manifest for image-family: runtime-v1 and runtime-v2.
3) Run a manual canary promotion for a single image family and validate Console coverage and rollback.
4) Enable automated phased promotions for non-critical images, monitor for 2 weeks, then extend to critical LTS channel images with security signoff.

Links & artifacts:
- Design sketch: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/RE-IMAGE-ROTATION
- Proof-of-concept SBOM-diff: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sbom-tools/pulls/82
- Staging runbook: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/release-engineering/rotation-runbook
- Security signoff ticket (pending): SEC-78
updates: 2025-02-21: Kickoff meeting with Release Eng, Infra, and Security. Agreed to reuse sbom-diff and image-catalog instead of building a new DB. Assigned Kofi as owner.
2025-02-25: Prototype synchronizer consumed CI event and produced signed SBOM delta for runtime-v2:sha256:abc123. Verified signature with release key in staging.

2025-03-01: Kernel sanity suite added to pre-promotion job; found transient GPU driver init hang on g5-type instance for one image variant. Filed ENG-14003 to track sanitizer fix for the image builder.

2025-03-03: Design review feedback from Console team: require rollout timeline links and SBOM diff link in the UI. Incorporated change; updated Console PR reference: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/456.
2025-03-04: Security requested audit trail for pinset changes; added requirement to sign pinset manifest and require security_approval for LTS promotions. Marked security_review_required=true.
